paragraphs: On Monday, September seventh, Mia sent Nadia an email with a photo of Snow. Snow was Mia's little white kitten. Nadia was a pen pal in Ms. Ong's class in Singapore. On Thursday afternoon, Mia still had no answer from Nadia. After school, she went to Lily's house with Snow in a small basket. The two girls sat on the sofa in the living room. Lily put her laptop on the low table. Pip lay near their feet with his red ball.

Mia opened the email page every ten minutes, but the page was always empty. "I'm nervous," said Mia. "Did Nadia receive my photo? I hope she did." "She hasn't answered yet, has she?" asked Mia. "No, she hasn't," said Lily. "Wait one more hour. You are not worried, are you?" "A little," said Mia. "I want an answer soon." Lily could see Mia's feelings on her face, and she wanted to help. "Nadia loves animals, doesn't she?" asked Lily. "Yes, she does," said Mia, "and she writes about them in every email." "Then she will love Snow," said Lily. Snow jumped out of the basket and played with Pip's red ball. Pip watched her with big eyes. Mia laughed, and for one minute she forgot the laptop. Then she looked at the empty page again.

At five o'clock, the laptop made a small sound. There was a new email from Nadia! Mia read it out loud to Lily. "Dear Mia, I am so glad you sent me a photo of Snow! She is wonderful, and I am pleased that you wrote to me. Please send me more photos soon. Best wishes, Nadia."

Mia jumped up from the sofa with a big smile. "Now I am happy!" said Mia. "Let's send Nadia a photo of Pip, too," said Lily. Pip wagged his tail when he heard his name. Snow came back to the sofa and went to sleep on Mia's lap. "Waiting is hard, but a good email makes me happy," said Mia.
text.summary: Mia waits at Lily's house for an email from her pen pal Nadia. Lily asks kind questions, and at five o'clock the answer comes.
